title: If / ElseIf / Else
summary: Conditional branching: run code only when a condition is truthy. Only `nil` and `false` fail the test — 0, "" and {} all pass. Luau also has if-expressions.

syntax:
if condition then
    -- runs when condition is truthy
elseif other then
    -- second chance
else
    -- fallback
end

-- Luau if-expression (value form):
local label = if rich then "💰" else "💸"
local x = if a then 1 elseif b then 2 else 3

details.heading: Truthiness rule
details.body: The condition passes for ANY value except `nil` and `false`. So `if 0 then` runs its body, and so does `if "" then`.

details.heading: No switch statement
details.body: Luau has no switch/case. Use elseif chains or a dispatch table (`handlers[key]()`).

explanation.whatItIs: The decision-maker. 'If the player has a key, open the door; otherwise, show a message.'
explanation.whyItExists: Almost every behavior depends on conditions — state, permissions, phase of the game.
whenToUse: Guard clauses at the top of functions: `if not player then return end`
If-expressions for picking one of two values inline
whenNotToUse: Deeply nested ifs (pyramid of doom) — prefer early returns or extracting functions
Long elseif chains over many discrete values — a dispatch table is cleaner
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
if doorOpen then        -- is this truthy?
    walkThrough()
elseif hasKey then      -- else, check this
    unlockDoor()
else                    -- otherwise
    knock()
end
```
Exactly ONE branch runs — the first true one, or else.
tips: Prefer positive condition names; `if not dead` reads worse than `if alive`
Guard-clause style (return early) keeps the main path at one indent level
`if a and b or c` as a ternary breaks when b is falsy — see logical operators
commonMistakes: Writing `else if` (with a space) instead of `elseif` — that opens a nested if and demands an extra `end`
Using `=` instead of `==` in the condition
Expecting `if 0 then` to skip — 0 is truthy in Luau

examples.title: Guards + if-expression
examples.code:
local function openDoor(player)
    if not player or not player.Character then
        return   -- guard: bail out early
    end

    local hasKey = player:FindFirstChild("Key") ~= nil

    if hasKey then
        print("Door opens!")
    else
        print("Locked. Find the key.")
    end

    -- if-expression picks a value:
    local message = if hasKey then "Welcome!" else "Locked."
    print(message)
end

examples.title: Dispatch table beats elseif chains
examples.code:
-- Instead of:
--   if cmd == "heal" then ... elseif cmd == "kick" then ... elseif ...

local commands = {
    heal = function(p) print("heal", p) end,
    kick = function(p) print("kick", p) end,
    tp   = function(p) print("tp", p) end,
}

local function handle(cmd, player)
    local fn = commands[cmd]
    if fn then
        fn(player)
    else
        warn("Unknown command:", cmd)
    end
end
